entry.title: 21052026 - Building Memories Brick by Brick
entry.summary: Short post about Lego activities and Sets with my girls.
entry.content:
Building Memories Brick by Brick

There are some things in life that matter more than success, money, or achievements — and for me, that is my daughters.

Watching them grow into their own unique people has been one of the greatest privileges of my life. They make me laugh, challenge me, inspire me, and remind me every day what truly matters. No matter how busy life gets, the moments I spend with them are the moments I value the most.

Discovering LEGO Together

One thing that has become especially special lately is LEGO.

My 15-year-old daughter absolutely loves building LEGO sets. What started as a fun hobby has turned into something much bigger — a shared experience that has brought us closer together.

There’s something surprisingly relaxing about slowly watching an entire city come to life one brick at a time.

So far, "S" has built three LEGO City sets, and every one of them has its own memories attached to it.

City sets we have at present

  • LEGO City Custom Police Car Garage: 60457
  • LEGO City Police Train Heist: 60508
  • LEGO City Explorers' Arctic Polar Express Train: 60470

Video links

  • LEGO City Trains running 1
  • LEGO City Trains running 2

More Than Just LEGO

But that’s the beauty of it.

It’s not really about the LEGO itself.

It’s about the time together.

In a world full of distractions, screens, stress, and constant noise, these simple moments matter more than ever.

As a parent, you eventually realize that the biggest memories are often created during the smallest moments.

  • Not during expensive holidays
  • Not during major milestones
  • But during ordinary evenings spent together doing something you both love

entry.title: My Mini Review
entry.content:
My brief review of Anycubic's water washable resin versus Esun's water washable resin.

In this brief comparison, I'll be sharing my thoughts on Anycubic's water washable resin versus Esun's water washable resin in white.

I found that Esun's water washable resin offers good value for its price, but it comes with a few drawbacks. One notable issue is that the prints tend to fade when exposed to sunlight during the curing process. Additionally, over time, these prints can develop unsightly cracks, which was rather disappointing. On a positive note, this resin proved easier to remove from supports and rafts compared to Anycubic's resin. However, I was somewhat let down by the color, as it leaned more towards a milky, creamy white rather than a crisp, bright white that would complement 3D printed models effectively.

On the other hand, I'm currently quite impressed with Anycubic's water washable resin. I have several models still in the process of printing on my 3D printer, and the quality is consistently high. The white hue is strikingly bright and appears to cure more effectively than Esun's counterpart.

For now, this concludes my initial assessment. I plan to follow up with another post, complete with images showcasing the differences between the prints, and I'll offer my final verdict based on my personal preference and how well each resin performs for my specific needs.

Links: anycubic esun
